summary: This note is a career summary of Preki, a Serbian-born soccer player. It covers his start at Red Star Belgrade and his five seasons with the Tacoma Stars, where he earned multiple awards. It then traces stints in Sweden, St. Louis, Everton, San Jose, and Portsmouth, ending with the Grizzlies buying his contract in 1995.
one_line: Career history of Serbian-born soccer player Preki, covering Tacoma Stars MISL honors, Everton, and San Jose Grizzlies CISL years.
key_facts: Preki was born in Serbia and played briefly for Red Star Belgrade in the old Yugoslav First League.
Preki came to Red Star Belgrade from FK Čukarički Stankom, where he played in the youth team.
In the summer of 1985, Tacoma Stars head coach Bob McNab spotted Preki at an indoor tournament in Belgrade and signed him.
Preki played five seasons for the Tacoma Stars.
Preki was a three-time First Team All Star with the Tacoma Stars.
Preki was the 1988 and 1989 All Star Game MVP.
Preki led the league in assists in 1988 and in scoring in 1989.
During the summer of 1989, Preki began considering becoming a U.S. citizen and returning to the outdoor game to become eligible for the U.S. national team.
Preki played one season for Råslätts SK in Sweden in 1990.
The Tacoma Stars released Preki in July 1990 as part of a salary reduction move.
In August 1990, Preki signed with the St. Louis Storm, where he played two seasons.
Everton manager Howard Kendall bought Preki for GBP 100,000 in the summer of 1992 following a trial.
Preki made 53 appearances for Everton, 28 of them as a substitute.
In June 1994, Preki signed with the San Jose Grizzlies of the Continental Indoor Soccer League, where he rejoined Bob McNab.
Preki played eight games for the San Jose Grizzlies, scoring sixteen goals, before returning to England in August 1994 to play for Portsmouth.
On July 5, 1995, the Grizzlies purchased Preki's contract from Portsmouth.
Preki was the CISL's second leading scorer and league MVP.
